citations.assessment: The Rif and Rosh directly give Rav Ashi and Rami bar Abba as father-in-law, in accord with Hullin. Both underlying readings are pinned.
The Rif and Rosh directly give Rav Ashi and Rami bar Abba as father-in-law, in accord with Hullin. Both underlying readings are pinned.
Rami bar Abba poses the question of reusing a synagogue’s materials. The checked text has Rav Pappa and an unqualified Rav Huna, both prohibiting it.
The checked Eruvin directly reads Rami bar Abba. Preserve Heilprin’s Ammi reading and his correction proposal as such.
The text has Rami bar Abba transmitting in Rav Huna’s name.
Eruvin has Rami bar Abba transmitting in Rav Assi’s name. The other statement on 100b has Rami bar Hama in Rav Assi’s name, so keep the two passages distinct.

Rif has the Ashi reading in the distinct second Eruvin teaching, attributing it to Mari bar Abba in the running text. For the first teaching Rif has Rabbah bar Rav Huna in Rav’s name. The checked Rosh uses Rav Assi for both and attributes each to Rami bar Hama. Adjudicate each wording separately.

Rif has the Ashi reading in the distinct second Eruvin teaching, attributing it to Mari bar Abba in the running text. For the first teaching Rif has Rabbah bar Rav Huna in Rav’s name. The checked Rosh uses Rav Assi for both and attributes each to Rami bar Hama. Adjudicate each wording separately.
The checked source names Rami bar Abba as the transmitter and repeats the institution formula twice, both citing R. Yosi.
Taanit first quotes Rami bar Abba. Rav Nahman then transmits Rabbah bar Avuha’s qualification.
The first reports the interval for blessing over the sea and the second the Euphrates blessing. Both are in R. Yitzhak’s name. The third statement there drops his name.
